newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina voters approve flurry of local bonds.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina voters approve flurry of local bonds.

text.p: North Carolina voters approved a wide variety of general obligation bond issues in city referendums, elections officials said Wednesday.

Greensboro, N.C., voters rejected a $2 million general obligation bond issue to finance improvements of the stadium used by the Greensboro Bats minor league baseball team. But they approved five other general obligation bond issues totalling $35 million.

In the city of Durham, N.C., voters approved five general obligation bond issues totalling $86.3 million, elections officials said. Approved were a $35.2 million issue for streets, a $20.4 million issue for parks and recreation, a $20 million housing bond issue, a $5.5 million issue for arts and museums, and a $5.2 million bond issue for public transportation.
Voters in Chapel Hill, N.C., approved a $13.5 million GO bond issue for parks, streets and sidewalks, Orange County officials said. The proposal passed with 12,649 yes votes and 6,993 no votes.
